1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## Quick start 42 43 Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear: 44 45 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 46 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 47 48 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 49 cacheComponents: true, 50 partialPrefetching: true, 51 } 52 53 export default nextConfig 54 ``` 55 56 To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption). 14	`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.

17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {

28

31	  cacheComponents: true,
32	  partialPrefetching: true,
33	}
34	```
35	
36	`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
37	
38	## Reference
39	
40	| Value   | Description                                 |
41	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
42	| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
43	| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |
44	
45	## How prefetches resolve
46	
47	Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
48	
49	With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
50	
51	The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
52	
53	> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
54	
55	A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
56	
57	> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
58	
59	## Per-segment overrides
60	
61	A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                     |
66	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
68

Done. Verified against a production build with real prefetch requests.

## What I changed

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled Partial Prefetching, which is what gives each route a shared App Shell and makes per-link prefetching available:

```ts
cacheComponents: true,
partialPrefetching: true,
```

**`app/page.tsx`** — the title depends on `params`, which the shared App Shell deliberately excludes (it's one shell reused by every link into the route). `prefetch={true}` opts each link into a per-link prefetch that resolves *that link's* URL data ahead of the click:

```tsx
<Link href={`/projects/${project.slug}`} prefetch={true}>
```

**`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — split the single component into two Suspense boundaries so the title can resolve at prefetch time independently, and put `await unstable_navigation()` above the details fetch. Everything below that call is left out of *both* prefetch stages and renders only on the navigation — so the details keep their `'use cache'` lifetime without being generated on every prefetch.

## Verified behavior

Probing `/projects/acme` at each of the three render stages against `next start`:

| Stage | Title | Description / activity |
|---|---|---|
| App Shell (default `<Link>`) | fallback only | fallback only |
| Per-link prefetch (`prefetch={true}`) | **"Acme Storefront"** | fallback only |
| Navigation | ✓ | ✓ |

So the title is in the payload before the click and paints instantly; the 800ms details request isn't issued until the user actually navigates, then streams into `Loading details...`. `next dev` reports no instant-validation insights for the route.

Two notes on incidental tree changes: `next dev` rewrote `AGENTS.md` to add its own managed `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` block (it re-adds this on every dev run), and `next build` added `.next/dev/types` to `tsconfig.json` plus generated `next-env.d.ts`. `PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>` resolves only from those generated types, so a bare `tsc --noEmit` on a clean checkout will report it as missing — the build's own TypeScript pass passes.
